newsitem.title: UK: London gold picks up after prices hold.
newsitem.headline: London gold picks up after prices hold.

text.p: Gold prices picked up from morning lows on Thursday afternoon, although dealers said they forecast they would soon renew the slide that has taken them down 3-1/2 percent since the start of the year.
They said trade buying and some short covering came into the market after New York opened and it became accepted that the price had weathered earlier selling.
Gold touched a low bid of $353.70 in early dealing.
"It looks like gold could consolidate today before the funds and speculators smack it down to $350, which is what they appear to have in mind," a London-based dealer said.
Bullion was fixed at $356.50 an ounce, up $2.00 on the morning fixing and just 10 cents below the level gained on Wednesday afternoon.
It has tumbled nearly $15 since the start of year when market weakness intensified.
Prices took a hit overnight in fund-driven selling out of New York and then Australian producer selling in Asia, dipping to below $354 an ounce at one point, dealers said.
"If producers are selling, they expect prices to decline further and want to lock in higher prices," an analyst said. "They're going to be selling into any small rally."
But physical offtake, mostly from the Middle East, was helping buoy prices in European trading, he added.

However, analysts said they saw little to support gold above $350 an ounce, which has not been seen since early October 1993. Silver and platinum both gained on gold's advance with the former seven cents higher at $4.72/$4.74, while platinum gained $2.50 to $361.50/$362.50.
Palladium continued its firmer trend with an afternoon fix of $122.25 up $2.25 overnight and matching the level on September 16, 1995.
"Prices are rising on consumer and speculative demand, amid Russian supply concerns," a London-based dealer noted.
Supply contracts between Japanese trade houses and Russia's platinum group exporting agency have not been signed, prompting Japanese traders to cover their needs in the spot market, dealers said.

"It looks like there will be a gap in delivery. I have heard the Russia might be going to miss out a month or might make up for it in a second month. It's not clear," an analyst said. Japan is the world's largest consumer of platinum group metals, including palladium, while Russia is the largest exporter of palladium. --Brian Spoors +44 171 542 2936
